chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There are five [women] whom the man can divorce in every state: the pregnant one, the one whom her husband has not had sexual relations with, the one whose husband is absent, the one who has not yet menstruated, and the one who has despaired of menstruation.

key_terms.عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ: In every state / at any time
key_terms.لَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: He did not enter/have relations with her

ai.seo_question: Which five types of women can be divorced at any time without waiting for menstruation?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the five categories of women exempt from the standard waiting period (iddah) constraints, permitting immediate divorce. This ruling is derived from the principle that the primary purpose of iddah—determining lineage or providing a cooling-off period—is either absent or fulfilled in these specific cases. It highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh where biological and marital status directly dictate the flexibility of divorce proceedings.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There are five whom the man can divorce upon every state – The pregnant, and the one whom her husband had not slept with, and the absentee from her husband, and the one who does not menstruate, and the one who has despaired from the menstruation (menopause)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Jamil ibn Darraj from ’Isma‘il al-Ju‘fiy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

A man can divorce five kinds of women in all conditions: They are pregnant women, women with whom one has not gone to bed, those whose husbands are absent, those who do not experience Hayd (menses) and those in their menopause.”’
